Similarly, a vendor's reported MLPerf software gain [@EassaEryilmaz2023H100MLPerfSoftware] holds only for the version pair that produced it, while at the physical end of the range, the Cougar Point correction [@Intel2011CougarPoint] shows that any containment strategy transfers only as far as the failure mechanism it can actually reach.

| **Transfer unit** | **Changed dependency** | **Valid action** | **Required target check** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Learned congestion predictor trained on specific process, library, and design family** | Target process, standard-cell library, netlist family, placement flow, or routed-result definition shifts. | Requalify unchanged predictor; recalibrate, adapt, retrain, or retire only after isolating what fails. | Measure class-specific target errors and decision quality against held-out routed target results. |
| **H100 results across MLPerf Training v2.1/v3.0, with vendor software attribution** [@EassaEryilmaz2023H100MLPerfSoftware] | Subsequent compiler, library, workload, or hardware generation alters configuration. | Constrain published improvement to reported versions/workloads; rerun comparison for new pair. | Repeat end-to-end workload measurement, pinning complete hardware and software configurations under identical result definitions. |
| **Cougar Point containment and correction results** [@Intel2011CougarPoint] | Target defect and remediation mechanisms differ. Intel required revised silicon and replacement programs. | For the reported SATA-degradation defect, distinguish temporary containment from the revised silicon needed for permanent correction. | Exercise corrected silicon and containment strategies against the target failure class before claiming correction. |
: **Transfer tests apply across learned, software, and physical components.** Actions follow changed dependencies, and target checks observe specific claimed failures or improvements. {#tbl-ch9-transfer-stress-tests tbl-colwidths="[22,26,24,28]"}

Transferring components does not alter decision rights. Automated systems propose or screen candidates within declared studies, while named architects and reviewers remain responsible for freezes, waivers, signoffs, and tapeout decisions (@sec-what-architect-owns). The source study structure and reference candidate can support target exploration, while the original source conclusion remains attached to the conditions that established it.

## Open Questions {#sec-patterns-open-questions}

Determining which architectural conclusions, learned surrogates, and verification evidence survive a move across workloads, compilers, process nodes, or packages exposes five open research problems:

- **How can a transfer study bound the risk of silently discarding its best target candidates?** Requalifying a source-trained screening surrogate on a small target sample catches false acceptances among the designs that advance, yet says nothing about viable architectures that the stale filter wrongly rejects before physical evaluation. When a workload shifts from dense matrix tiles to irregular sparse attention or a floorplan moves to a new metal stack, a conservative surrogate can prune the exact structural novelties the target problem requires without raising an error flag. Auditing a random subset of rejected candidates with a reference simulator or place-and-route flow can expose those missed opportunities, but every audit consumes budget that could otherwise evaluate top-ranked proposals. The open problem is how to couple shift-aware uncertainty estimation with sequential audit allocation so a team can bound its worst-case missed performance gain as the search distribution itself evolves.

- **When does a microarchitectural advantage survive a change in compiler scheduling?** Pinning the compiler snapshot makes a source-to-target comparison reproducible, yet also locks in scheduling heuristics that may favor one candidate by accident. An accelerator can outperform its baseline simply because its scratchpad capacity and systolic dimensions divide evenly into a Triton or Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) loop-tiling pass, meaning the measured gain belongs to a fragile alignment between one datapath and one lowering heuristic rather than a durable hardware improvement. Perturbing problem dimensions or re-tuning schedules for each candidate can expose brittle wins, but running a full compiler autotuner inside every hardware evaluation quickly exhausts the search budget. The research challenge is to design low-cost sensitivity probes and schedule-invariant representations that separate intrinsic datapath capability from compiler alignment before the hardware interface is frozen.

- **Which parts of a learned physical predictor can be factorized from a specific process node?** The transfer map separates a circuit representation from the numerical relationships fitted on top of it, yet most graph-based timing and congestion surrogates entangle netlist topology with the cell delays, metal pitches, and pin-access rules of a single process design kit. When a design migrates from FinFET to gate-all-around nanosheets or adopts a backside power delivery network, that entanglement invalidates the model's wire-parasitic and routing predictions even when the register-transfer level structure is unchanged. Much as sim-to-real robotics transfer separates invariant rigid-body kinematics from surface-specific actuator adapters, a circuit representation that isolates technology-invariant logical connectivity from node-specific physical calibration layers could dramatically reduce the number of routed target layouts needed to requalify the predictor, provided the adapted surrogate preserves worst-case slack and congestion rankings near the signoff boundary.

- **How can a transfer harness bound the physical reach of an incremental design change?** Selective requalification saves engineering time only when the dependency map isolates every claim a target change can disturb. Incremental timing analysis[^fn-incremental-sta-c09] updates arrival times along modified logic cones [@OpenROADDocs], yet repositioning an SRAM macro or resizing a tile buffer can also perturb clock-tree insertion delay, capacitive crosstalk, and dynamic voltage drop across neighboring blocks that share no logical wires with the edited module. Relying purely on structural netlist connectivity understates the affected slice, whereas rerunning full-chip extraction and electrothermal signoff after every localized edit erases the economic advantage of modular transfer. The open problem is how to combine fast physical-sensitivity bounds with structural dependency graphs to certify when an unedited neighbor's timing and power evidence remains valid.

[^fn-incremental-sta-c09]: **Incremental static timing analysis**: An optimization in physical design signoff where timing graphs are updated only for logic cones and net parasitics directly affected by an incremental circuit or placement modification, rather than recomputing the full chip. In a transfer setting, an incremental update understates the change if macro repositioning alters global clock-tree insertion delay or coupling on neighboring paths that the update treats as undisturbed.

- **When can block-level architectural conclusions compose across chiplet and packaging boundaries?** Chiplets joined by die-to-die links such as Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) promise modular hardware reuse, where pre-qualified compute dies and memory controllers assemble into new product tiers without full-chip redesign. Even when each die's internal RTL and local timing closure carry forward intact, partitioning a shared coherence domain or systolic dataflow across package substrates introduces protocol-adapter latency, bump capacitance, and thermal coupling between stacked or adjacent dies. Monolithic performance and power models miss those boundary penalties, while full multi-die cosimulation is too slow for early exploration. The research question is what interface-level abstractions and compositional contracts allow an architect to predict when a block-level advantage will survive disaggregation into a multi-die package before committing to substrate routing and thermal verification.

## Summary {#sec-patterns-summary}

The transfer test turns source-to-target differences into a plan for requalification or a new architectural study. An admission check asks whether the decision itself survived the move; four stages then assign each unit an action and pair changed dependencies with checks able to observe the resulting risk. In the prospective Lighthouse application (@sec-cross-stack-pattern-transfer), simulator outputs and candidate identities remain useful historical material, while workload coverage, the executable software path, memory costs, and implementation behavior still require target evidence. Exploration can reuse source work while leaving room to generate and evaluate different hardware and software organizations when the target requires them. The one measured case in the book's own record points the same way, since a ranking of two array shapes survived a workload transposition while its margin did not.

::: {.callout-takeaways}
- **Components move, conclusions do not.** Data sources, models, tool paths, and checks remain reusable while their invariants and dependencies hold; a source conclusion remains applicable only where its supporting conditions still hold. Changed or uncertain dependencies require new evidence.
- **Check the decision before the components.** An admission check asks whether the question itself changed; unit actions and target checks follow only once that is settled, and a changed question reopens every claim tied to it.
- **Materiality is claim-specific.** A change reopens a claim when it alters the candidate identity, executable path, measured quantity, objective, decision rule, ranking, constraint verdict, or physical mechanism; magnitude alone decides nothing.
- **Transfer benefit needs a matched arm.** A carried prior earns its place only against a target-only arm with the same tasks, budgets, and stopping rules, with adaptation and requalification charged to the transfer.
- **A transferred result carries its compiler version.** Retain hardware and software snapshots with the inputs and procedures needed to repeat a comparison, and test software sensitivity before attributing a gain to microarchitecture, since a comparison that pins the hardware but not the toolchain can mistake compiler maturity for a hardware gain.
:::

The next step is to evaluate the complete approach across repeated, varied, and adversarial architectural studies (@sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). The source-to-target map identifies which claims each changed study must establish. Those comparisons can then test whether an AI-native design system improves the architecture result, reduces the total engineering cost of achieving it, or does both.
